result: Wrote `docs/research/emergence-deeper-2026-09-24.md` only. The five interface lines: 1. Always mark the last move’s squares, and when a piece is selected show legal destinations as dots (Chess.com and Lichess board highlights / piece destinations). 5. Cut “busywork” UI and clutter that hides the idea you want the player to think about; keep difficulty that is about the real board idea (Blow’s good vs bad difficulty).

description: Record why shots need no bonus
result: **Finding:** In `src/ai/search.ts`, the main search builds legal moves with `genLegal(..., 'all')` via `genPiece`, then `apply`s each before scoring the child. Ordinary captures and archer shots both put victims in `captures` (shots use `to === from`); `apply` clears those squares, so the material change is already on the next position. Ogre shoves are separate moves (`captures: []` plus `shove`); `apply` relocates the piece (and under `push` moves the ogre onto the vacated square) but removes nothing, so material does not change—yet the search can still pick them. Quiescence only generates `captures`, so shots are in Q-search and shoves are not. Do not add a shot or shove bonus: shots are already driven by material, shoves already show up without a shove-target term, and either bonus would be a new unmeasured value. `docs/research/eval-sees-shots-2026-09-24.md`

description: How to pre-approve agent actions
result: Here’s what the **current** Cursor docs say (2026). Older names like YOLO / Ask Every Time / Auto-Run still show up in older pages and forums; the live setting is named below. --- ## 1. Auto-run / YOLO / sandbox — where it lives now **Path:** **Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution** (Also written as **Settings → Cursor Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution**.) Sources: [Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Terminal integration](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/terminal), [Auto-review Run Mode](https://cursor.com/changelog/auto-review). **Run Mode** choices (Cursor 3.6+): | Mode | What it does | |------|----------------| | **Auto-review** | Recommended default. Allowlisted calls run right away. Other shell commands run in the **sandbox** when they can. Anything else is checked by the Auto-review classifier. | | **Allowlist** | Only allowlisted actions skip approval. Sandboxing for shell is optional (“Allowlist with sandboxing”). | | **Run Everything** | Every tool call runs with no prompts. No sandbox. | **Name changes (don’t look for these anymore as primary modes):** - **Ask Every Time** — deprecated in 3.5; for the same behavior use **Allowlist** with an empty allowlist. - **Run in Sandbox** — folded into **Allowlist** with sandboxing on. - **YOLO** — not a current documented mode name; the “approve everything” option is **Run Everything**. **Chat composer control:** Official docs only point to **Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution**. They do **not** document a separate Run Mode picker in the chat composer. Approval happens on the **approval card** in chat when something still needs you. **Sandbox network modes** (same Run Modes page): **sandbox.json Only**, **sandbox.json + Defaults** (default), **Allow All**. --- ## 2. Command allowlist — stop asking for the same command **In Settings** 1. Open **Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution**. 2. Use the terminal / **Command allowlist** (entries like `npm`, `git status`, `vitest`). 3. Or put the same list in `~/.cursor/permissions.json` / project `.cursor/permissions.json` as `terminalAllowlist`. Source: [permissions.json reference](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/permissions). **On the approval card** Docs name the action **Add to allowlist**. When `permissions.json` owns that allowlist, the in-app editor is read-only and **Add to allowlist** is hidden. In the product/UI, people also see **Always Run** (e.g. Always Run `'git'`) for the same idea—add that command so it stops prompting. Prefer specific entries (`vitest`, `npm test`) over a bare `git` if you can. **MCP:** Same place conceptually — `mcpAllowlist` or the in-app MCP allowlist; format `server:tool` (e.g. `github:*`). --- ## 3. Can Auto-review / “smart” approval cards be turned off or pre-approved? **You choose the mode; you don’t fully “pre-approve Auto-review.”** - Stay on **Auto-review** → fewer prompts, but the classifier can still block, and if the agent insists you still get an **approval prompt**. Docs say Auto-review is **best-effort**, not a hard security wall ([Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Governing agent autonomy with Auto-review](https://cursor.com/blog/agent-autonomy-auto-review)). - Switch to **Allowlist** → no classifier; only allowlist (+ optional sandbox) decides. - Switch to **Run Everything** → no approval cards for tool calls (highest risk). - Steer Auto-review with plain English in `permissions.json` → `autoRun.allow_instructions` / `autoRun.block_instructions` (steering only, not a guarantee). **What still asks even when a mode would otherwise auto-run** ([Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Agent Security](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security)): | Still needs you | Why | |-----------------|-----| | Commands that **can’t use the sandbox** | e.g. writes outside the workspace, privileged ops — Cursor shows they’re outside the sandbox and asks. | | **Network** beyond sandbox policy | Sandbox network is limited unless you open it (defaults / `sandbox.json` / Allow All). | | **Browser Protection** | Browser tools don’t auto-run. | | **File-Deletion Protection** | Deletes (including `rm`) still need approval. | | **External-File Protection** | Create/modify/delete **outside** the workspace still needs approval. | | **Configuration files** | Workspace code edits usually auto-apply; config/settings-style files need approval. | | **MCP** | After connecting a server, each tool call still needs approval unless it’s on the MCP allowlist. | | Classifier block → agent retries with you | Auto-review can still surface a normal approval card. | **Ordinary workspace file edits and reading/searching** do **not** need Allow by default ([Agent Security](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security)). **Subagents:** [Subagents](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents) does not describe a separate “Allow subagent” toggle. Shell/MCP/Fetch they run still follow the same Run Mode / approvals. --- ## 4. Safest setup that cuts Allow clicks for normal local tests (vitest, edits) Plain steps: 1. Open **Cursor Settings**. 2. Go to **Agents → Approvals & Execution**. 3. Set **Run Mode** to **Auto-review** (not **Run Everything**). 4. Leave sandbox network on **sandbox.json + Defaults** unless you need more. 5. Keep **Browser Protection**, **File-Deletion Protection**, and **External-File Protection** on. 6. When vitest/`npm test`/`pnpm` still prompts once, use **Add to allowlist** / **Always Run** for that command — or add `vitest`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `node` under the Command allowlist in the same settings page. 7. Optional: ask the agent to add soft guidance in `permissions.json`, e.g. allow tests/linters, block AWS/git push — only works in **Auto-review**. That is the setup Cursor itself recommends as the “safest useful” default: **Auto-review** + sandbox + allowlist for repeat safe commands, without turning every guard off ([Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Security and Privacy Hardening](https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise/security-hardening)). **Avoid for day-to-day coding:** **Run Everything** — zero prompts, no sandbox. --- ### Quick “where did it go?” | Old / informal name | Now | |---------------------|-----| | YOLO / auto-run everything | **Run Everything** | | Ask every time | Empty **Allowlist** | | Run in Sandbox | **Allowlist** + sandboxing | | Settings → Agents → Auto-Run (older Browser docs) | Prefer **Approvals & Execution** for Run Mode; Browser page may still say **Agents → Auto-Run** for browser allow/block lists | Doc titles cited: **Run Modes**, **Agent Security**, **permissions.json reference**, **Terminal integration**, **Auto-review Run Mode**, **Browser**, **Governing agent autonomy with Auto-review**, **Security and Privacy Hardening**.
